object_description: well-proportioned three-storey building with offset levels
design_condition: The building is positioned to reinforce the paved playground as the center, connect smoothly to park-like open spaces, and follow the raised edge of the existing main building with an arcade and split-level entrances.

positive.statement: The three-storey, well-proportioned building integrates into the existing complex and creates appropriate open spaces.
The upper-floor arrangement of classrooms, stairs and atriums is simple and clear.
The staircase connected to the atriums creates identity and meets the fire-protection requirements.
The atriums and anterooms basically enable an expansion of lessons, with the anterooms particularly suitable for exhibitions and gatherings.
The compact organization and simple supporting structure are expected to be very cost-effective.
The outdoor spaces are appropriately sized and well designed.

negative.statement: The staggered entrances create floor-level shifts that lead to spatial and operational complications.
Several rooms have low heights that are not approvable and are not reasonable.
The anterooms are only of limited suitability for group work because stair access passes through them and creates disruption potential.
The offset hinders internal relationships more than it adds value, despite producing economically interesting compactness.
The massive architectural expression is hardly able to create an appropriate dialogue with the slenderness and delicacy of the existing architecture.
Despite good external-space conditions, the building appears too independent and does not sufficiently complement and strengthen the existing ensemble.
